Zero planning *.md files cite WO-188-D015. standard-pass-2026-10-19.md:490-491 says the operator-word advisories are historical. Inspection supports the implied contradiction. The flagged records quote the operator verbatim with no digest: WO-200-D002 'Extend the test repair scope', WO-210-D024 'ok if it doesn't, i authorize failing…', WO-221-D028 'Approve both acceptance corrections'. All three were committed before the pass closed (899eeec1). The baseline and those records are unchanged since then, so the check already counted these as current, not historical, when the pass called them historical. One point dissents. The settled follow-up FUP-71fc2efc208f597a in followups.json does route D015, but its reopen condition is narrower ('a typed quotation without a digest'), and D015's rejected option admits that the regex cannot tell paraphrase from quotation. That narrows how to read the trigger. It does not falsify what the reproduction shows.

attempts.reason: The reproduction ran in the episode TMPDIR and shows what it claims. A copy made with the same clone flags as freezeSubject (clone --no-hardlinks --no-checkout, then checkout --detach) keeps origin pointing at its source. A push from the copy created branch 'escaped' in the source. Both fingerprints stayed at the empty-input hash e3b0c44298fc before and after the push: the source's tracked status (porcelain, --untracked-files=no) and its untracked list. The frozen copy's own origin resolves to the live operator checkout <home>/Projects/DotLn. Reading the code confirms the probe matches the real mechanism. freezeSubject never removes or rewrites origin. The filing guard checks only trackedStatus, which is `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`. The witnesses for claude-cli-print are the copy and temporary inventories, and both skip .git. So nothing that binds the receipt would see a ref or object written into the source repository through the copy's origin. I did not push to the real origin; that path is shown only by remote get-url and the code.
